title: The naive cotangent complex of a presentation commutes with localization at one element
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $P=A[x_s,\ s\in S]$ a polynomial ring over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and $\alpha:P\to B$ a surjective homomorphism of $A$-algebras with kernel $I$. For such a presentation write $\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)$ for the two-term complex of $B$-modules $I/I^2\to\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB$, $f\bmod I^2\mapsto\mathrm df\otimes1$ ($\Omega$ and $\mathrm d$ as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]). Let $g\in B$, let $B_g$ be the localization of $B$ at the powers of $g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], choose $f\in P$ with $\alpha(f)=g$, and let $\beta:P[x]\to B_g$ be the homomorphism of $A$-algebras which is $\alpha$ followed by $B\to B_g$ on $P$ and sends the new variable $x$ to $1/g$; let $J=\ker\beta$. Then $\beta$ is surjective, $J$ is generated by $I$ and $fx-1$, and: (1) $J/J^2=(I/I^2)_g\oplus B_g\,(fx-1)$ as $B_g$-modules, where $(I/I^2)_g=I/I^2\otimes_BB_g$ maps to $J/J^2$ by the map induced by $I\subseteq J$, and the second summand is free of rank $1$ on the class of $fx-1$; (2) $\Omega_{P[x]/A}\otimes_{P[x]}B_g=(\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB_g)\oplus B_g\,\mathrm dx$; (3) these decompositions can be chosen so that $\mathrm{NL}(\beta)\cong\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)\otimes_BB_g\oplus(B_g\xrightarrow{\ g\ }B_g)$ as complexes of $B_g$-modules. In particular, since $g$ is a unit of $B_g$, the map $(I/I^2)_g\to\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB_g$ of $\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)\otimes_BB_g$ is injective if and only if the map $J/J^2\to\Omega_{P[x]/A}\otimes_{P[x]}B_g$ of $\mathrm{NL}(\beta)$ is injective, and the two maps have isomorphic cokernels.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 08JZ (lemma-principal-localization-NL, line 35605) and its proof (lines 35632-35689); the final sentence of 08JZ (the canonical map NL_{B/A} (x)_B B_g -> NL_{B_g/A} is a homotopy equivalence) is not part of this node. Used in Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CE (smoothing.tex lines 381-392: the presentations A_a = R[x_0,...,x_n]/(hx_0 - 1, I))

proof.text: ($\beta$ is surjective and $J=IP[x]+(fx-1)P[x]$.) Let $\alpha[x]:P[x]\to B[x]$ apply $\alpha$ to the coefficients ($x\mapsto x$); by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-coefficient-map-kernel] (with $f:=\alpha$, $T=\{x\}$) it is surjective with kernel $I\cdot P[x]$. Let $\lambda:B[x]\to B_g$ be the $B$-algebra map with $x\mapsto1/g$; by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-polynomial-quotient] (with $R:=B$, $r:=g$) it is surjective with kernel $(gx-1)B[x]$. The $A$-algebra maps $\lambda\circ\alpha[x]$ and $\beta$ agree on the variables $x_s$ and $x$, so $\beta=\lambda\circ\alpha[x]$ by the universal property of the polynomial ring $P[x]=A[x_s,x]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Hence $\beta$ is surjective, and $J=\alpha[x]^{-1}\bigl((gx-1)B[x]\bigr)$. Since $\alpha[x](fx-1)=gx-1$: if $h\in J$, write $\alpha[x](h)=(gx-1)q$ and choose $q'\in P[x]$ with $\alpha[x](q')=q$; then $h-(fx-1)q'\in\ker\alpha[x]=IP[x]$. Conversely $I$ and $fx-1$ lie in $J$. So $J$ is generated by $I$ and $fx-1$, and $P[x]/J\cong B_g$ via $\beta$; in particular $J/J^2$ is a $B_g$-module.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 08JZ (lemma-principal-localization-NL), line 35632: 'Since P[x]/(I, fx - 1) = B[x]/(gx - 1) = B_g we get the statement about I and fx - 1 generating J'

proof.text: (Clause (2).) By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-polynomial-extension] (with $R:=A$, $A:=P$, $e=1$, $z_1=x$, so $B=P[x]$) the $P[x]$-linear map $(P[x]\otimes_P\Omega_{P/A})\oplus P[x]\to\Omega_{P[x]/A}$, $(c\otimes\mathrm dp,c')\mapsto c\,\mathrm dp+c'\,\mathrm dx$, is an isomorphism. Applying $-\otimes_{P[x]}B_g$ and using $(P[x]\otimes_P\Omega_{P/A})\otimes_{P[x]}B_g=\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB_g$ (associativity of $\otimes$) gives $\Omega_{P[x]/A}\otimes_{P[x]}B_g=(\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB_g)\oplus B_g\,\mathrm dx$, where $\mathrm dp\otimes b$ in the first summand is the element $\mathrm d_{P[x]/A}(p)\otimes b$ for $p\in P\subseteq P[x]$, and the second summand is free with basis $\mathrm dx\otimes1$. Write $\mathrm{pr}:\Omega_{P[x]/A}\otimes_{P[x]}B_g\to B_g$ for the coordinate along $\mathrm dx$; it vanishes on the first summand.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 08JZ (lemma-principal-localization-NL), lines 35634-35652 (top row of the diagram; 'the element dx ... provides a splitting for the top row')

proof.text: (The map $\iota$, and generators of $J/J^2$.) $\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)\otimes_BB_g$ is the complex $(I/I^2)_g=I/I^2\otimes_BB_g\to(\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB)\otimes_BB_g=\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB_g$, $\bar a\otimes b\mapsto\mathrm da\otimes b$. The inclusion $I\subseteq J$ induces the $B$-linear map $I/I^2\to J/J^2$, $a\bmod I^2\mapsto a\bmod J^2$ ($B$ acting on $J/J^2$ through $B\to B_g$, step 1), whose $B_g$-linear extension is $\iota:(I/I^2)_g\to J/J^2$, $\bar a\otimes b\mapsto b\,(a\bmod J^2)$. By step 1 every $h\in J$ is $\sum_ip_ia_i+q(fx-1)$ with $a_i\in I$, $p_i,q\in P[x]$, so $h\bmod J^2=\sum_i\beta(p_i)(a_i\bmod J^2)+\beta(q)[fx-1]$: hence $J/J^2=\iota\bigl((I/I^2)_g\bigr)+B_g[fx-1]$, $[fx-1]$ the class of $fx-1$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 08JZ (lemma-principal-localization-NL), lines 35633-35647 (bottom row of the diagram: (I/I^2)_g -> J/J^2 -> (gx-1)/(gx-1)^2 -> 0)

proof.text: ($\iota$ is injective.) This is [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-conormal-injective] for the data $A\to B$, $\alpha$, $g$, $\beta$ of the statement.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 08JZ (lemma-principal-localization-NL), lines 35661-35672 ('Let us prove (I/I^2)_g -> J/J^2 injective')

proof.text: (The differential of $\mathrm{NL}(\beta)$ on the generators.) The map of $\mathrm{NL}(\beta)$ is $\delta_\beta:J/J^2\to\Omega_{P[x]/A}\otimes_{P[x]}B_g$, $h\bmod J^2\mapsto\mathrm dh\otimes1$. For $a\in I$, $\mathrm d_{P[x]/A}a$ is by step 2 the element $\mathrm da$ of the first summand, so $\delta_\beta(\iota(\bar a\otimes b))=\mathrm da\otimes b=(\delta_\alpha\otimes B_g)(\bar a\otimes b)$ lies in $\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB_g$ and $\mathrm{pr}\circ\delta_\beta\circ\iota=0$. By the Leibniz rule and $\mathrm d1=0$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], $\mathrm d(fx-1)=x\,\mathrm df+f\,\mathrm dx$; as $\beta(x)=1/g$ and $\beta(f)=g$, $\delta_\beta[fx-1]=g^{-1}(\mathrm df\otimes1)+g\,\mathrm dx$, so $\mathrm{pr}(\delta_\beta[fx-1])=g$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 08JZ (lemma-principal-localization-NL), lines 35684-35688 ('d(fx - 1) = x df + f dx = g(g^{-2} df + dx) in Omega_{P[x]/A} (x) B_g')

proof.text: (Clause (1).) Let $\xi\in(I/I^2)_g$ and $b\in B_g$ with $\iota(\xi)+b[fx-1]=0$. Applying $\mathrm{pr}\circ\delta_\beta$ and step 5 gives $bg=0$; $g$ is a unit of $B_g$, so $b=0$, then $\iota(\xi)=0$ and $\xi=0$ by step 4. With step 3: $J/J^2=\iota\bigl((I/I^2)_g\bigr)\oplus B_g[fx-1]$, $\iota$ maps $(I/I^2)_g$ isomorphically onto the first summand, and $b\mapsto b[fx-1]$ is injective, so the second summand is free of rank $1$ on $[fx-1]$. (Stacks obtains the freeness from the image $g\,\mathrm dx$ of $gx-1$ in $\Omega_{B[x]/B}\otimes B_g$; $\mathrm{pr}$ is that map composed with the identification $\Omega_{B[x]/B}\otimes B_g=B_g\,\mathrm dx$.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 08JZ (lemma-principal-localization-NL), lines 35648-35655 and 35674-35682

proof.text: (Clause (3).) Put $e=g^{-2}(\mathrm df\otimes1)+\mathrm dx$. The $B_g$-linear automorphism of $(\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB_g)\oplus B_g\,\mathrm dx$ (step 2) that is the identity on the first summand and sends $\mathrm dx\mapsto e$ (inverse: $\mathrm dx\mapsto\mathrm dx-g^{-2}(\mathrm df\otimes1)$) shows $\Omega_{P[x]/A}\otimes_{P[x]}B_g=(\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB_g)\oplus B_g\,e$ with $B_g\,e$ free on $e$. By step 5, $\delta_\beta[fx-1]=g\,e$ and $\delta_\beta\circ\iota=\delta_\alpha\otimes B_g$ into the first summand. So with respect to $J/J^2=(I/I^2)_g\oplus B_g[fx-1]$ (step 6) and this decomposition, $\delta_\beta=(\delta_\alpha\otimes B_g)\oplus(b\mapsto gb)$: the maps $\iota\oplus(b\mapsto b[fx-1])$ in degree $1$ and $\mathrm{id}\oplus(c\mapsto ce)$ in degree $0$ form an isomorphism of complexes $\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)\otimes_BB_g\oplus(B_g\xrightarrow{g}B_g)\cong\mathrm{NL}(\beta)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 08JZ (lemma-principal-localization-NL), lines 35674-35689 ('Thus we have a short exact sequence of two term complexes ... we can take as splittings ...')

proof.text: (The 'in particular'.) For a direct sum of maps $\varphi\oplus\psi$ one has $\ker(\varphi\oplus\psi)=\ker\varphi\oplus\ker\psi$ and $\operatorname{coker}(\varphi\oplus\psi)=\operatorname{coker}\varphi\oplus\operatorname{coker}\psi$. Multiplication by the unit $g$ on $B_g$ is bijective, so by step 7 $\ker\delta_\beta\cong\ker(\delta_\alpha\otimes B_g)$ and $\operatorname{coker}\delta_\beta\cong\operatorname{coker}(\delta_\alpha\otimes B_g)$; in particular $\delta_\alpha\otimes B_g$ is injective if and only if $\delta_\beta$ is.
